question_text: He gave up smoking last year. Choose the correct meaning of the phrasal verb.
explanation: 'Give up' means to stop doing something.

question_text: The meeting was called off.
She broke down during the interview.
explanation: 'Break down' means to lose control emotionally.

question_text: The car broke down on the highway.
explanation: 'Break down' for a machine means to stop working.

question_text: I need to look up the word in the dictionary.
explanation: 'Look up' means to search for information.

question_text: Please put off the lights before leaving.
The teacher pointed out my mistakes.
explanation: 'Point out' means to identify or explain.

question_text: He takes after his father.
We need to come up with a plan.
explanation: 'Come up with' means to produce or invent.

question_text: She ran into an old friend at the mall.
I can't put up with this noise anymore.
The plane took off on time.
He turned down the job offer.
I need to work out the solution.
explanation: 'Work out' means to solve or calculate.

question_text: She gave in to the pressure.
explanation: 'Give in' means to surrender or yield.

question_text: The burglar got away before the police arrived.
I'm looking forward to seeing you.
explanation: 'Look forward to' means to anticipate eagerly.

question_text: He came across an old photograph.
explanation: 'Come across' means to find by chance.

question_text: You should carry out the instructions carefully.
explanation: 'Carry out' means to execute or perform.

question_text: I will take care of the problem.
She made up the whole story.
explanation: 'Make up' means to invent a story.

question_text: The teacher told us to hand in our assignments.
The soldiers were ordered to fall in.
explanation: 'Fall in' means to form a line.

question_text: The manager decided to do away with the old rules.
Their car ran out of petrol.
explanation: 'Run out of' means to use up completely.

question_text: He brushed up on his French before the trip.
explanation: 'Brush up on' means to improve or refresh knowledge.

question_text: The teacher told him to keep up the good work.
The thief was let off with a warning.
explanation: 'Let off' means to release without severe punishment.

question_text: She came down with a cold.
explanation: 'Come down with' means to become ill.

question_text: He is about to give in to their demands.
The committee put forward a new proposal.
The meeting was put off until next week.
They called for the resignation of the chairman.
The plane is about to take off.
She looks up to her older sister.
He fell out with his best friend.
The meeting has been brought forward to Tuesday.
explanation: 'Bring forward' means to reschedule to an earlier time.

question_text: She has taken up a new hobby.
explanation: 'Take up' means to start a new activity.

question_text: The government has done away with the tax.
He was put down by the critic's remarks.
The ship set out for Europe at dawn.
The bomb went off in the market.
The light went out suddenly.
He put on his coat and left.
She took off her shoes before entering.
The meeting came to an end at noon.
explanation: 'Come to an end' means to conclude.

question_text: He is looking after his sick mother.
The teacher gave out the exam papers.
She has given up her seat to an elderly man.
They ran after the thief.
The fire was put out by the firefighters.
He is not able to get by on his salary.
explanation: 'Get by' means to survive with limited resources.

question_text: She is going through a difficult time.
The manager turned up late for the meeting.
The old building was pulled down.
The doctor advised him to cut down on sugar.
She was brought up by her grandmother.
explanation: 'Bring up' means to raise a child.

question_text: The workers walked out over the pay dispute.
explanation: 'Walk out' means to go on strike.

question_text: He made off with the stolen money.
explanation: 'Make off with' means to escape with something.

question_text: She broke into tears when she heard the news.
explanation: 'Break into tears' means to start crying.
